principle: Published tariff labels are canonical. A traveler label may resolve only when equivalence to exactly one published tariff identity is explicitly reviewed. Otherwise it must fail closed and request clarification.

sourceBackedCanonicalNotes.label: Charlotte Amalie
sourceBackedCanonicalNotes.reason: The published tariff uses Charlotte Amalie as the table endpoint. Generic Town is not promoted to this endpoint by this policy.

sourceBackedCanonicalNotes.label: Airport Terminal
sourceBackedCanonicalNotes.reason: The published tariff separately names Airport Terminal / Cyril E. King Airport context. Broad Lindbergh Bay is a geographic area and is not treated as the airport terminal.

sourceBackedCanonicalNotes.label: Dorothea
sourceBackedCanonicalNotes.reason: The explicit Red Hook relationship publishes Dorothea, while the main table separately publishes Dorothea Estate, Dorothea Lower, and Dorothea Upper with different fares. These identities must not collapse.

sourceBackedCanonicalNotes.label: Havensight
sourceBackedCanonicalNotes.reason: Published tariff identities distinguish Havensight (crossroad) and Havensight (WICO); generic Havensight is financially ambiguous.

completionInterpretation: Canonical endpoint audit is complete when every published source endpoint remains addressable as its exact governed identity and every non-reviewed broad/ambiguous traveler label fails closed. Completeness does not require inventing aliases for ambiguous labels.
